chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: Brother presses college; University of Detroit and the Mirror Ballroom
summary: His brother Glenn urges college again; while he plays a year's contract at Detroit's Mirror Ballroom and goes to the University of Detroit, Isham Jones buys the band.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And not only that, my brother is after me to go to college.
Glenn?
Again?

Yeah, he's never given up. And he -- my mother, said well Glenn's still after him, so he came up and -- to Chicago again, and talked to me and I said, 'Well if by chance maybe I can do it.' So at the end of that summer, in August, I worked with -- had a band was formed, I think, out of Minneapolis. And, we worked in a place near Detroit. And the band was very good, we had arrangements and everything going for them. So, we got a call-- a year's contract at the Mirror Ballroom in Detroit. I thought this is perfect, a year, boy, I'll walk out of this great, I'll have all this experience in playing, for dancing and I can do this -- so Johnny Carlson was the first trumpet player, who later was the first trumpet player with Isham Jones, who -- this is the story, he convinced me -- I was rooming with him, and he said, 'Why don't you go out and go to school, University of Detroit's here and --

why don't you register?" I said, all right, maybe I will. He said, I'll drive you out. He had a car. We got up the next morning, I went out to the University of Detroit, I applied, they took me and I went to -- I started school. College. AT the University of Detroit. And I was -- I had three 8:00 o'clock classes. A week and worked in a ballroom till 1:00. Everynight. Besides studying, doing rehearsals, used to do all these things.
So, finally, this same office, Stevens and [With] called me and said, how's it going. I said, well I don't know. I'd call up Tiboo and said, boy, that's a rough -- End of Reel I
Now where we broke off there -- ah,
I went to --
You -- you said about -- yeah.

Well Johnny Carlson took me out and I got I was going to school. So, Stevens called me and said Isham Jones was coming back in the business and was looking for a band that was already organized. And would I be interested because I told Jack Tiboo on the telephone it was getting pretty rough. So I didn't know whether I'd stay in college, but he said, "Well, you know your family, I think you'd better stay." This -- before this happened. So Isham Jones flew up, heard the band and liked it. So they want said, do you want to sell it? So they took the band and I stayed in school. And I give up the contract at the Mirror Ballroom.
Oh.
And that's the start of his band --
Oh, for heaven's sake.
Johnny Carlson was his lead trumpet player. And all the guys that were in that band, stayed with that band.
That was the Isham Jones band?
Yeah. And he went from there I think --
That was a beautiful band.

-- to Milwaukee, the Wisconsin Hotel in Milwaukee -- I think later that's where Woody joined him and made these changes. All the guys around the midwest -- he had the guys that I had. Red Ballard was in that band.
Well --
Red Ballard who later was with Benny Goodman.
Yes.
Yeah, Red Ballard was in that band. Who else: Oh, I don't know a bunch of guys that I know from Minneapolis.
Well did you -- did you regret that?
